scenarios.name: witness_and_controller_report
scenarios.note: A witness of the identifier, signing as its non-transferable key, and the controller, signing with the keys of its inception, each report the state at the inception; both notices are kept, one per source.

scenarios.name: notices_against_the_local_log
scenarios.note: A notice of a state ahead of the local log is kept, since nothing local contradicts it. Once the log has caught up, a notice of an earlier state is stale, and one whose latest event is not the local event at that number is refused.

scenarios.name: notice_from_an_unknown_signer
scenarios.note: A transferable source reports a state before its own inception is known; the notice waits in the reply escrow and is kept once the inception is accepted.

scenarios.name: notices_not_signed_by_their_source
scenarios.note: A notice whose signature does not verify, and one signed by someone other than the source its route names, are not kept.

scenarios.name: trusted_sources_only
scenarios.note: With keripy's trust policy on, a notice is kept only from the identifier itself, one of its witnesses, or a watcher a local identifier configures; a stranger's is refused.

divergence_older_notice.name: older_notice_after_a_newer_one
divergence_older_notice.note: A witness reports the state after the interaction, then, in a reply made earlier, the state at the inception. keripy looks up the earlier reply from that source by the reported event's SAID, which is not what it stores replies under, so it finds none, compares no dates, and keeps the older report. The port compares the reply dates and refuses it.
